findings.issue: The 35-word lead ('Here you see how brands like yours took a brief through sampling…') and the aqua REQUEST A QUOTE pill still stand on the photo under the two-line title, although the site rule puts a lead much longer than the competitor's under the hero.
findings.reference: The competitor's page this one follows (About Swimwear Bali) is a factory photo carrying only the white H1, with no lead and no button; its copy starts on white under the photo.
findings.fix: Apply the reference page type's on-photo lead limit to general pages (heroText.leadWords: 0 for the about reference), so PageHero.astro's heroLeadShown() moves the /case-studies/ lead and its button into the block under the hero and only the H1 stays on the photo.

findings.issue: On phones the lead runs to four lines of small white text across the sitter's body, between the three-line title and the large aqua pill, so the whole lower half of the hero is text over the photo.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero carries only the white H1 over the photo, and its text follows under it on white.
findings.fix: Apply the same per-reference lead limit in PageHero.astro (heroLeadShown()) at every width, so the lead and button stand under the phone hero.

findings.issue: Still unfixed: the two order-case cards sit in a narrow centred column covering about the middle half of the 1440 frame, under 'A recent order', whose heading starts on the content's left edge, so the cards float mid-page with about 350 px of empty space on each side instead of following their heading.
findings.reference: The competitor's content starts on the content's left edge under its heading and fills the content width; it never centres outlined cards in a narrow column.
findings.fix: In the shared patterns.css, stop centring `.order-cases` when headings start on the left: under `body[data-heading-align="start"]` set `.order-cases { margin-inline: 0; }`, or better, set the cases side by side in equal columns starting at the content's left edge, sized to the copy rather than to a fixed width.

findings.issue: On phones the wide CTA photo is cropped to a tall card, so the subject's face sits right behind the heading 'Talk to Our Factory About Your Brand' and her body behind the lead, and the photo reads only as a dark smudge under the text.
findings.reference: The competitor sets text over photos only on an empty or calm part of the picture, never across a face.
findings.fix: Give the cta band a separate crop for narrow widths (art-direction), with the subject low or to one side, so the heading and lead fall on an empty part of the photo.

findings.issue: Still unfixed: the open first answer is one unbroken paragraph of about 370 words, about 40 lines on a phone and a dense 10-line block in the desktop column, covering three client projects, certifications and shipping terms in one run.
findings.reference: The competitor's body copy comes in short paragraphs of a few lines each.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, split the answer into short paragraphs (one per project, then one for certifications, testing and shipping), or shorten it and point to the cases section.

findings.issue: Still unfixed: on phones the question 'Have you worked with small start-up brands placing their first order, like us?' breaks at the compound's hyphen, so one line ends on 'start-' and the next begins with 'up brands'.
findings.reference: The competitor's headings and questions keep each word whole on its line.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, write 'start-up' with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011), or reword it as 'small new brands'.
